messages:
maria_support: Heads up — support queue getting multiple HTTP 503/500 reports this morning from hosted-api. Appears correlated to upstream runner exits (exit code 137). customer-impact: timeouts and duplicate retry billing for a handful of high-QPS customers. Logs pasted below.

 tzeng_oncall: Copy — can you paste the runner logs + affected region/model? Any deploys recently?

 maria_support: Region: us-west-2, model: rwd-infer-small-v2 (quantized). Error snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] worker[pid=32841] Killed signal 9 (SIGKILL) exit code 137
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] runtime: CUDA OOM during attention kernel: requested 1.2GiB free, available 640MiB
[2026-03-17T09:12:04Z] cgroup: memory cgroup invoked OOM-killer: kill process 32841 (runner)
```
Also docker events show container restart count bumped to 4 in 3m.

 jake_engineer: That looks like host-level memory cgroup eviction after a big spike in KV prefetch/batch. Did autoscaler kick? Any recent quant swap or kernel change?

 maria_support: Autoscaler logged a spike but couldn't provision fast enough; we saw many concurrent requests with long contexts (context_len ~ 12k tokens) and increased batch_size headers (bs=24) from Customer X. We had a quant-swap deploy last night at 02:00 UTC (image: rwd-runtime:quant-2026-03-16).

 emma_pm: We shuffled a couple of baseline models to quant-swap channel yesterday (small sample of hosts) — maybe the canary leaked. I'm flagging rollout but need eng to confirm.

 jake_engineer: Ok. Immediate mitigation options:
- mark hosts with repeated exit code 137 UNHEALTHY in router
- lower default max_batch_size for quant runtime to 8
- enable fallback routing to rwd-infer-small-v2-cpu for affected customers
I'll open a PR to change router heuristic + healthcheck TTL. Anyone can apply manual workaround now?

 tzeng_oncall: I can flip the route override for the top-impacted customer in us-west-2 to fallback CPU cluster and temporarily throttle per-connection QPS to 5. Want me to proceed?

 customer_ops: Please proceed — Customer X is already calling in. Also we have billing duplicates: retries are counted as new tokens causing double charges when requests time out and client retries.

 maria_support: Proceeded with fallback + throttle. After the change, 503s for Customer X dropped from 60/min to ~3/min. But other customers still seeing flakiness. Need longer-term fix.

 jake_engineer: Repro steps (local):
```
# stress script: spawn 30 concurrent requests with large context
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-infer-small-v2","input":"<12k-token-payload>","batch_size":24}' &
done
```
When I run against a quantized runner image on a GPU with 12GB memory it OOMs in 40-60s.

 sre_bot: Noted. Kernel and driver versions on affected hosts: nvidia-driver 525.105, kernel 5.15.0-101. No automated rollback yet.

 jake_engineer: Plan: (1) revert quant-swap image on canary hosts (hotfix PR), (2) tighten router healthcheck for exit code 137, (3) add temporary autoscale faster scale-up policy for us-west-2, (4) audit billing for duplicate retries and issue credits. I'll own 1+2. ETA 2h.

 maria_support: Thanks. I'll keep CS notified and collect any additional logs. Customer X agreed to a short scheduled failover window.

 tzeng_oncall: Executed manual throttle+fallback. Monitoring latency and 503 rate.

 maria_support: Update 09:35 UTC — after throttle + fallback overall 503s down 82% in us-west-2. Leaving thread open for followups and billing audit. :white_check_mark:
